docs.title: Contributing to STEMAIDE
docs.text: We love contributions! Whether you are an educator, student, or engineer, you can help us build the best open-source STEM curriculum in Africa.

docs.title: Ways to Contribute
docs.text:
1. Report Bugs: Found a typo or a broken circuit diagram? Open an issue on GitHub.
  2. Add Translations: Help us translate these guides into local languages (Twi, Ga, Ewe, Swahili, etc.).
  3. Create Missions: Design a new project and add it to the curriculum (See the Contributing to the Curriculum guide).

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
1. Fork this repository.
  2. Clone your fork.
  3. Create a branch: git checkout -b my-new-mission.
  4. Commit your changes.
  5. Push to the branch.
  6. Submit a Pull Request.

docs.title: Community Code of Conduct
docs.text: Be respectful, inclusive, and helpful. We are here to learn together.

docs.title: 6. Push Your Changes
docs.text:
Now that you’ve made and saved your changes, you’ll need to push them to your forked repository.

  1. Stage your changes:
git add .
  1. Commit your changes with a meaningful message:
git commit -m "Added contribution guide and updated changelog"
  1. Push your changes to your fork:
git push origin update-readme

docs.title: 7. Create a Pull Request
docs.text:
A pull request (PR) is how you ask to merge your changes into the main repository.

  1. Go to your forked repository on GitHub.
  2. Click on the Pull Requests tab.
  3. Click on the New Pull Request button.
  4. Select your branch (e.g., update-readme) and compare it with the main repository’s branch (usually main or master).
  5. Add a title and description for your PR:
    • Title: Added Contribution Guidelines
    • Description: Describe the changes you made, e.g., “Added detailed steps for contributing and updated the changelog.”
  6. Click Create Pull Request.

docs.title: 8. Wait for Review
docs.text:
The project maintainers will review your pull request. Here’s what might happen:

  1. Approved: Your changes will be merged into the main project!

  2. Requested Changes: Maintainers might ask for modifications. Follow their feedback and update your PR.

  3. To update your PR after feedback:

    • Make the required changes in your local branch.
    • Commit and push the changes:
    git add .
git commit -m "Fixed feedback issues"
git push origin update-readme

docs.title: Additional Tips
docs.text:
- Ask for Help: If you’re stuck, feel free to ask for help by commenting on your pull request or opening an issue.
- Test Your Changes: Ensure that your changes look correct by previewing them in your text editor or GitHub.

Congratulations! 🎉 You’ve successfully contributed to the project. Thank you for making this documentation better for everyone!

docs.title: About STEMAIDE
docs.text: Reinventing the Future. We are an EdTech startup empowering young Africans through immersive, hands-on STEM education experiences.

docs.title: Our Mission
docs.text:
We exist to equip young Africans with the 21st-century creative mindset and the technical skills they need to become the next generation of Innovators and Entrepreneurs.

We believe in a practical, hands-on approach. We don't just teach theory; we build the future.

docs.title: What Does "STEMAIDE" Stand For?
docs.text:
It is more than just an acronym. It is our pedagogical framework:

🔬 STEM

Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics. The fundamental laws of the universe and the tools to manipulate them.

🎨 Arts

Creativity is at the heart of engineering. We blend aesthetics with function to build beautiful solutions.

💡 Innovation

We don't just repeat what exists. We invent new ways to solve old problems.

📐 Design

Design Thinking is our process. Empathize, Define, Ideate, Prototype, Test.

🚀 Entrepreneurship

We solve problems for people. We teach students to turn their inventions into viable solutions for their communities.

Community leaders are responsible for clarifying and enforcing our standards of acceptable behavior and will take appropriate and fair corrective action in response to any behavior that they deem inappropriate, threatening, offensive, or harmful.

Community leaders have the right and responsibility to remove, edit, or reject comments, commits, code, wiki edits, issues, and other contributions that are not aligned to this Code of Conduct, and will communicate reasons for moderation decisions when appropriate.

All community leaders are obligated to respect the privacy and security of the reporter of any incident.

docs.title: Mission 1.1: First Light
docs.text: Role: Lab Apprentice Objective: Take control of the system. Send your first command to the microcontroller.

docs.title: Result Preview
docs.text: The LED will turn ON for 1 second, then OFF for 1 second.

docs.title: 1. The Call to Adventure
docs.text:
Welcome to The Lab. Before you can build smart cities, you must first master the flow of electricity.

Your challenge is simple but critical: Command the board to create light. If you succeed, you prove that you are ready to be an Engineer.

docs.title: 2. The Toolkit
docs.text:
Retrieve these items from your kit:

  • 1x Arduino Uno (The Brain)
  • 1x LED (The Output - Any color)
  • 2x Jumper Wires (Red & Black)
  • 1x Breadboard (The Workbench)

docs.title: 3. The Blueprint
docs.text:
Construct the circuit exactly as shown.

  • Positive Leg (Long) -> Pin 6 (The Signal)
  • Negative Leg (Short) -> GND (The Ground)

[!IMPORTANT] Check your Polarity! If the LED is backwards, it won't light up. The Long Leg must go to Power (Pin 6).

docs.title: 4. The Logic
docs.text:
We communicate with the board using C++. Here is the step-by-step logic:

  1. Define: Give Pin 6 the name ledPin.
  2. Setup: Tell the Arduino "Pin 6 is for Talking (OUTPUT), not Listening".
  3. Loop:
    • Turn Power ON (HIGH).
    • Wait 1 second.
    • Turn Power OFF (LOW).
    • Wait 1 second.

docs.title: The Code
docs.text:
// Mission 1.1: First Light

const int ledPin = 6; // We are using Pin 6

void setup() {
  // Prepare the pin to send signals out
  pinMode(ledPin, OUTPUT);
}

void loop() {
  digitalWrite(ledPin, HIGH); // Turn ON (5V)
  delay(1000);                // Wait 1 second
  digitalWrite(ledPin, LOW);  // Turn OFF (0V)
  delay(1000);                // Wait 1 second
}

docs.title: Explaining the lines
docs.text:
• int ledPin = 6; -> We create a variable named ledPin and set it to 6. Now, whenever we say ledPin, the computer knows we mean Pin 6.
  • pinMode(ledPin, OUTPUT); -> Pins can be inputs (listening) or outputs (talking). We want to talk to the LED, so we set it to OUTPUT.
  • digitalWrite(ledPin, HIGH); -> Send 5V to the pin. Let there be light!

docs.title: 5. Upload & Test
docs.text:
1. Click Verify (Checkmark).
  2. Click Upload (Arrow).
  3. Look at your board. Is the LED on?

docs.title: 6. Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• LED not turning on?
  • Try flipping the LED. Remember, the Long leg must go to Pin 6.
  • Check if the wires are pushed all the way in.
  • Check if you uploaded the code successfully (Look for "Done uploading").
  • Dim light?
  • Ensure you are using a digital pin (0-13), not an analog pin.

docs.title: 7. Extensions & Upgrades
docs.text:
Challenge: Can you make it blink faster?

  • Hint: Change the delay(1000) to delay(200).
  • Upgrade: Add a second LED on Pin 5 and make them blink like a Police Car (Alternating).

docs.title: Mission 1.10: The Knight Rider
docs.text: Role: Automotive Engineer Objective: Create a back-and-forth light scan.

docs.title: Result Preview
docs.text: Lights pulse from 1 to 5, then back from 5 to 1.

docs.title: 1. The Call to Adventure
docs.text: You've built signals and runway guides. Now, it's time for fluid motion. Your mission is to create a "Scanner" effect where the light bounces back and forth like a famous crime-fighting car.

docs.title: 2. The Toolkit
docs.text:
• 5x LEDs (Red, White, Yellow, Green, Blue)
  • 1x Arduino Uno
  • 10x Jumper Wires
  • 1x Breadboard

docs.title: 3. The Blueprint
docs.text:
• Signal Pins: 6, 5, 4, 3, 2
  • GND: Common Ground

docs.title: 4. The Logic
docs.text:
Algorithm:

  1. Forward: Pulse Pin 6 -> 5 -> 4 -> 3 -> 2.
  2. Reverse: Pulse Pin 3 -> 4 -> 5 -> 6.

docs.title: The Code
docs.text:
// Mission 1.10: The Knight Rider
int pins[] = {6, 5, 4, 3, 2};

void setup() {
  for(int i=0; i<5; i++) {
    pinMode(pins[i], OUTPUT);
  }
}

void loop() {
  // 1. Move Forward
  for(int i=0; i<5; i++) {
    digitalWrite(pins[i], HIGH);
    delay(100);
    digitalWrite(pins[i], LOW);
  }

  // 2. Move Backward
  for(int i=3; i>0; i--) { // Start at green (3rd index)
    digitalWrite(pins[i], HIGH);
    delay(100);
    digitalWrite(pins[i], LOW);
  }
}

docs.title: 5. Upload & Test
docs.text:
1. Upload the code.
  2. Does the light "bounce" off the ends of the breadboard?
  3. Upgrade: Change the delay to 50 for a high-speed scan.

docs.title: 6. Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Stuck at one end? Check your logic—did you forget to turn the LED LOW before moving to the next one?
  • Wired backwards? If the scan starts at the Blue LED instead of the Red, simply swap your pin numbers in the pins[] array.

docs.title: Mission 1.2: The Heartbeat
docs.text: Role: Lab Apprentice Objective: Make the circuit "come alive" with a steady pulse.

docs.title: Result Preview
docs.text: The LED will turn ON for 1 second, then OFF for 1 second.

docs.title: 1. The Call to Adventure
docs.text: A steady light proves power is flowing, but a blinking light proves your code is pulsing. Your mission is to program the "Heartbeat" of your first machine.

docs.title: 2. The Toolkit
docs.text:
• 1x LED (Red)
  • 1x Arduino Uno
  • 2x Jumper Wires
  • 1x Breadboard

docs.title: 3. The Blueprint
docs.text:
• Positive Leg (Long) -> Pin 6
  • Negative Leg (Short) -> GND

docs.title: 4. The Logic
docs.text:
Algorithm:

  1. Define: Use Pin 6 for the LED.
  2. Setup: Set the pin to OUTPUT.
  3. Loop:
    • HIGH (ON) for 1000ms.
    • LOW (OFF) for 1000ms.

docs.title: The Code
docs.text:
// Mission 1.2: The Heartbeat
const int ledPin = 6;

void setup() {
  pinMode(ledPin, OUTPUT);
}

void loop() {
  digitalWrite(ledPin, HIGH); // Light ON
  delay(1000);                // Wait 1 second
  digitalWrite(ledPin, LOW);  // Light OFF
  delay(1000);                // Wait 1 second
}

docs.title: 5. Upload & Test
docs.text:
1. Upload the code.
  2. Does the LED blink steadily?
  3. Experiment: Change delay(1000) to delay(100). What happens to the "Heartbeat"?

docs.title: 6. Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Light stays ON? You might have forgotten the LOW command or the second delay.
  • Light stays OFF? Check if the LED is pushed all the way into the breadboard.

docs.title: Mission 1.3: Twin Stars
docs.text: Role: Power Grid Engineer Objective: Light up multiple zones at once.

docs.title: Result Preview
docs.text: Both LEDs turn ON and stay ON.

docs.title: 1. The Call to Adventure
docs.text: One light is a signal. Two lights are a system. Your mission is to double the power and control two independent lights simultaneously.

docs.title: 2. The Toolkit
docs.text:
• 2x LEDs (Red & White)
  • 1x Arduino Uno
  • 4x Jumper Wires
  • 1x Breadboard

docs.title: 3. The Blueprint
docs.text:
• LED 1 (Red): Pin 6 (+) to Pin 6, (-) to GND.
  • LED 2 (White): Pin 5 (+) to Pin 5, (-) to GND.

docs.title: 4. The Logic
docs.text:
Algorithm:

  1. Define: Use Pin 6 and Pin 5.
  2. Setup: Set both pins to OUTPUT.
  3. Loop: Turn both HIGH.

docs.title: The Code
docs.text:
// Mission 1.3: Twin Stars
const int led1 = 6;
const int led2 = 5;

void setup() {
  pinMode(led1, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(led2, OUTPUT);
}

void loop() {
  digitalWrite(led1, HIGH);
  digitalWrite(led2, HIGH);
}

docs.title: 5. Upload & Test
docs.text:
1. Upload the code.
  2. Do both project lights glow?
  3. Challenge: Can you make just one turn off while the other stays on?

docs.title: 6. Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Only one light is on? Check the wires for the one that is off. Does it have both a Power wire and a Ground wire?
  • Colors looking weird? Ensure you didn't mix up the Positive and Negative legs of the second LED.

docs.title: Mission 1.4: The Alternator
docs.text: Role: Signal Technician Objective: Create an alternating warning signal.

docs.title: Result Preview
docs.text: Red ON / White OFF -> White ON / Red OFF.

docs.title: 1. The Call to Adventure
docs.text: Emergency vehicles use alternating lights to grab attention. Your mission is to create a "Police Style" signal by flipping between two LEDs.

docs.title: 2. The Toolkit
docs.text:
• 2x LEDs (Red & White)
  • 1x Arduino Uno
  • 4x Jumper Wires
  • 1x Breadboard

docs.title: 3. The Blueprint
docs.text:
• Red LED: Pin 6
  • White LED: Pin 5
  • GND: Common Ground

docs.title: 4. The Logic
docs.text:
Algorithm:

  1. State A: Red HIGH, White LOW. Wait.
  2. State B: Red LOW, White HIGH. Wait.

docs.title: The Code
docs.text:
// Mission 1.4: The Alternator
const int red = 6;
const int white = 5;

void setup() {
  pinMode(red, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(white, OUTPUT);
}

void loop() {
  // State A
  digitalWrite(red, HIGH);
  digitalWrite(white, LOW);
  delay(500);

  // State B
  digitalWrite(red, LOW);
  digitalWrite(white, HIGH);
  delay(500);
}

docs.title: 5. Upload & Test
docs.text:
1. Upload the code.
  2. Does the light "jump" between the two LEDs?
  3. Speed Up: Change delay(500) to delay(100) for a faster strobe effect.

docs.title: 6. Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Both blink at the same time? Check your code—did you forget to set the other one to LOW in each step?
  • One light is much brighter? LEDs have different power needs. This is normal, but double check your wiring if one is barely glowing.

docs.title: Mission 1.5: The Triple Beam
docs.text: Role: Power Grid Monitor Objective: Manage high-output zones by lighting three LEDs simultaneously.

docs.title: Result Preview
docs.text: Red, White, and Yellow LEDs turn ON.

docs.title: 1. The Call to Adventure
docs.text: The main grid is expanding. You now need to manage three power zones at once. Your mission is to prove that your brain (Arduino) can handle the load of three simultaneous signals.

docs.title: 2. The Toolkit
docs.text:
• 3x LEDs (Red, White, Yellow)
  • 1x Arduino Uno
  • 6x Jumper Wires
  • 1x Breadboard

docs.title: 3. The Blueprint
docs.text:
• Red: Pin 6
  • White: Pin 5
  • Yellow: Pin 4
  • GND: Common Ground for all.

docs.title: 4. The Logic
docs.text:
Algorithm:

  1. Define: Pins 6, 5, and 4.
  2. Setup: All three to OUTPUT.
  3. Loop: Turn all three HIGH.

docs.title: The Code
docs.text:
// Mission 1.5: The Triple Beam
const int z1 = 6;
const int z2 = 5;
const int z3 = 4;

void setup() {
  pinMode(z1, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(z2, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(z3, OUTPUT);
}

void loop() {
  digitalWrite(z1, HIGH);
  digitalWrite(z2, HIGH);
  digitalWrite(z3, HIGH);
}

docs.title: 5. Upload & Test
docs.text:
1. Upload the code.
  2. Verify: Are all three zones glowing bright?
  3. Experiment: Change the code so only the middle light stays on.

docs.title: 6. Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Yellow light isn't working? Check Pin 4. Yellow LEDs are sometimes sensitive to the amount of power.
  • Breadboard mess? As you add more lights, the wires can get tangled. Try to keep them straight and organized to avoid "Short Circuits".

docs.title: Mission 1.6: The SOS Beacon
docs.text: Role: Rescue Specialist Objective: Create a sequence of emergency signals.

docs.title: Result Preview
docs.text: Red flashes -> White flashes -> Yellow flashes (Cycle).

docs.title: 1. The Call to Adventure
docs.text: Communication is vital during a rescue. If you can't speak, you use light. Your mission is to program a three-stage light sequence that signals for help at different levels of urgency.

docs.text:
• 3x LEDs (Red, White, Yellow)
  • 1x Arduino Uno
  • 6x Jumper Wires
  • 1x Breadboard

// Mission 1.13: The Manual Trigger
const int buttonPin = 2;
const int ledPin = 6;

void setup() {
  pinMode(ledPin, OUTPUT);
  // INPUT_PULLUP enables the internal brain resistor
  pinMode(buttonPin, INPUT_PULLUP);
}

void loop() {
  // Read the button state
  int isPressed = digitalRead(buttonPin);

  if (isPressed == LOW) { // LOW means the button is pressed!
    digitalWrite(ledPin, HIGH);
  } else {
    digitalWrite(ledPin, LOW);
  }
}

// Mission 1.16: The Shield Override
const int btn = 13;
const int layers[] = {12, 9, 4, 2};

void setup() {
  for(int i=0; i<4; i++) {
    pinMode(layers[i], OUTPUT);
  }
  pinMode(btn, INPUT_PULLUP);
}

void loop() {
  if (digitalRead(btn) == LOW) {
    // Shield ACTIVE (Blinking)
    for(int i=0; i<4; i++) digitalWrite(layers[i], HIGH);
    delay(500);
    for(int i=0; i<4; i++) digitalWrite(layers[i], LOW);
    delay(500);
  } else {
    // Shield STANDBY (All OFF)
    for(int i=0; i<4; i++) digitalWrite(layers[i], LOW);
  }
}

docs.title: 1. The Call to Adventure
docs.text: Bats navigate in total darkness by bouncing sound off walls. We call this Echolocation. Your mission is to build a high-tech distance sensor for a car that uses this same principle to prevent collisions.

docs.title: 3. The Blueprint
docs.text:
Ultrasonic Pins:

  • VCC -> 5V | GND -> GND
  • Trig -> Pin 9 | Echo -> Pin 10

RGB Pins:

  • R -> Pin 3 | G -> Pin 5 | B -> Pin 6

docs.title: 4. The Logic
docs.text:
Algorithm:

  1. Trig: Send a sound pulse.
  2. Echo: Measure how long it takes to come back.
  3. Math: Convert time into Centimeters.
  4. Reaction: If < 10cm, turn the light RED. Otherwise, keep it BLUE.

docs.title: The Code
docs.text:
// Mission 1.35: The Bat's Ear
const int trigPin = 9;
const int echoPin = 10;
const int red = 3;
const int blue = 6;

void setup() {
  pinMode(trigPin, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(echoPin, INPUT);
  pinMode(red, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(blue, OUTPUT);
  Serial.begin(9600);
}

void loop() {
  // 1. Send the Pulse
  digitalWrite(trigPin, LOW);  delayMicroseconds(2);
  digitalWrite(trigPin, HIGH); delayMicroseconds(10);
  digitalWrite(trigPin, LOW);

  // 2. Measure Echo
  long duration = pulseIn(echoPin, HIGH);
  int distance = duration * 0.034 / 2;

  // 3. React
  if (distance < 10) {
    digitalWrite(red, HIGH);

docs.title: Mission 2.1: The Bat's Warning
docs.text: Role: Neighborhood Engineer Objective: Build a proximity alarm that warns us when danger is too close.

docs.title: Result Preview
docs.text: As your hand gets closer (<20cm), the Warning LED turns ON.

docs.title: 1. The Call to Adventure
docs.text:
In the Neighborhood, blind corners are dangerous. Cars and pedestrians crash because they can't "see" what's coming.

We need a system that acts like a Bat: sending out sound waves to detect obstacles in the dark. If something gets too close, the Alarm (LED) must trigger.

docs.title: 2. The Toolkit
docs.text:
• 1x Ultrasonic Sensor (HC-SR04): The "Bat Eyes".
  • 1x LED: The Warning Light.
  • 4x Jumper Wires: For the Sensor.

docs.title: 3. The Blueprint
docs.text:
The Ultrasonic Sensor has 4 pins. Be careful!

  • VCC -> 5V
  • GND -> GND
  • Trig (Trigger) -> Pin 11 (Sends the shout)
  • Echo (Listener) -> Pin 12 (Hears the echo)
  • LED Positive -> Pin 13

docs.title: 4. The Logic
docs.text:
We communicate with the board using C++. Here is the step-by-step logic:

  1. Define: Variables for trigPin (11), echoPin (12), and ledPin (13).
  2. Speak: Send a "Shout" signal (Trig HIGH for 10 microseconds).
  3. Listen: Wait for the "Echo" signal to return.
  4. Math: Calculate distance: Distance = (Time x Speed) / 2.
  5. Decision:
    • IF Distance < 20cm -> Turn LED ON.
    • ELSE -> Turn LED OFF.

docs.title: The Code
docs.text:
// Mission 2.1: The Bat's Warning
const int trigPin = 11;
const int echoPin = 12;
const int ledPin = 13;

long duration;
int distance;

void setup() {
  pinMode(trigPin, OUTPUT); // Mouth (Speaks)
  pinMode(echoPin, INPUT);  // Ear (Listens)
  pinMode(ledPin, OUTPUT);
  Serial.begin(9600);       // Open Communications to PC
}

void loop() {
  // 1. Clear the throat
  digitalWrite(trigPin, LOW);
  delayMicroseconds(2);

  // 2. SHOUT! (Send sound wave)
  digitalWrite(trigPin, HIGH);
  delayMicroseconds(10);
  digitalWrite(trigPin, LOW);

  // 3. LISTEN (Measure how long it takes to return)
  duration = pulseIn(echoPin, HIGH);

  // 4. Calculate Distance (Speed of sound is 0.034 cm/us)
  distance = duration * 0.034 / 2;

  // 5. Logic: Is it too close? (< 20cm)
  if (distance < 20) {
    digitalWrite(ledPin, HIGH); // DANGER! Turn ON.
  } else {
    digitalWrite(ledPin, LOW);  // Safe. Turn OFF.
  }

  // Debugging: Print to screen
  Serial.print("Distance: ");
  Serial.print(distance);
  Serial.println(" cm");
}

docs.title: 5. The Debrief

docs.title: 6. Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Distance always 0?
  • Check your wires. Did you swap Trig and Echo?
  • Ensure VCC is connected to 5V (not 3.3V).
  • LED not working?
  • Check if it is inserted correctly (Long leg to Pin 13).
  • Check the serial monitor to see if the distance is actually below 20.

docs.text: Role: Sleep Technologist Objective: Build an alarm that wakes you up when the sun rises.

docs.title: Result Preview
docs.text: Light hits sensor -> Alarm BEEPS.

docs.title: 1. The Call to Adventure
docs.text: Waking up to a loud alarm in the dark is terrible. Your mission is to build a gentle alarm that only triggers when it sees natural light.

docs.text:
Algorithm:

  1. Sleep: Wait for Light > 500 (Morning).
  2. Wake Up: Trigger Buzzer.
  3. Snooze: Silence if light drops again (e.g., covered by a pillow).

docs.title: The Code
docs.text:
// Mission 2.10: Sunrise Alarm
const int ldrPin = A0;
const int buzzerPin = 2; // Fixed from legacy 'DO_PIN' confusion

void setup() {
  pinMode(buzzerPin, OUTPUT);
  Serial.begin(9600);
}

void loop() {
  int brightness = analogRead(ldrPin);
  Serial.println(brightness);

  // If it's bright (Daytime)
  if (brightness > 500) {
    // Beep Beep!
    digitalWrite(buzzerPin, HIGH);
    delay(100);
    digitalWrite(buzzerPin, LOW);
    delay(100);
  } else {
    // Shhh... sleeping
    digitalWrite(buzzerPin, LOW);
  }
}

// 1. Define Pins
const int redPin = 3;
const int greenPin = 5;
const int bluePin = 6;
const int ldrPin = A0;

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(9600);

  // 2. Configure Output Pins
  pinMode(redPin, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(greenPin, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(bluePin, OUTPUT);
}

void loop() {
  // 3. Read Light Level (0 to 1023)
  int lightLevel = analogRead(ldrPin);

  Serial.print("Light Level: ");
  Serial.println(lightLevel);

  // 4. Logic: Dark vs Bright
  // (Adjust '500' based on your room's light)

    setColor(255, 255, 255);
  } else {
    // BRIGHT: Turn OFF
    setColor(0, 0, 0);
  }

}

  analogWrite(redPin, red);
  analogWrite(greenPin, green);
  analogWrite(bluePin, blue);
}

docs.title: Mission 2.12: Smart Night Mode
docs.text: Role: City Operations Manager Objective: Modify the traffic lights. At night, they should save energy and just blink yellow.

docs.title: Result Preview
docs.text: Daytime -> Normal Cycle (R-Y-G). Night -> Blinking Yellow.

docs.title: 1. The Call to Adventure
docs.text: In the middle of the night, waiting for a green light when no one is around is annoying. Major cities switch to "Caution Mode" (Blinking Yellow) at night. Your mission is to automate this using the LDR.

docs.title: 4. The Logic
docs.text:
Algorithm:

  1. Check Light Level.
  2. IF Dark (< 300):
    • Blink Yellow (ON 500ms, OFF 500ms).
  3. ELSE (Day):
    • Run Standard Traffic Cycle (Red -> Green -> Yellow).

docs.title: The Code
docs.text:
// Mission 2.12: Smart Night Mode
const int ldrPin = A0;
const int red = 5;
const int yellow = 6;
const int green = 7;

void setup() {
  pinMode(red, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(yellow, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(green, OUTPUT);
  Serial.begin(9600);
}

void loop() {
  int brightness = analogRead(ldrPin);

  if (brightness < 300) {
    // NIGHT MODE: Blink Yellow
    digitalWrite(red, LOW);
    digitalWrite(green, LOW);

    digitalWrite(yellow, HIGH);
    delay(500);
    digitalWrite(yellow, LOW);
    delay(500);
  } else {
    // DAY MODE: Normal Cycle
    // Red
    digitalWrite(red, HIGH);
    delay(2000);
    digitalWrite(red, LOW);

    // Green
    digitalWrite(green, HIGH);
    delay(2000);
    digitalWrite(green, LOW);

    // Yellow
    digitalWrite(yellow, HIGH);
    delay(1000);
    digitalWrite(yellow, LOW);
  }
}

docs.title: 4. The Logic
docs.text:
Algorithm:

  1. Listen: Read measurement.
  2. Trigger: If loud (> threshold), toggle the state variable.
  3. Act: If state is 1, Light HIGH. If state is 0, Light LOW.

docs.title: The Code
docs.text:
// Mission 2.13: Clap Switch
const int soundPin = A0;
const int ledPin = 8;
int lightState = 0; // 0=Off, 1=On

void setup() {
  pinMode(ledPin, OUTPUT);
  Serial.begin(9600);
}

void loop() {
  int noise = analogRead(soundPin);
  Serial.println(noise); // Use this to calibrate

  // Threshold check (Adjust 600 based on serial monitor)
  if (noise > 600) {
    // CLAP DETECTED!
    if (lightState == 0) {
      lightState = 1;
    } else {
      lightState = 0;
    }

    // Wait for the clap to finish (Debounce)
    delay(500); 
  }

  // Update light based on state
  if (lightState == 1) {
    digitalWrite(ledPin, HIGH);
  } else {
    digitalWrite(ledPin, LOW);
  }
}

// Mission 2.14: Voice Commander
const int soundPin = A0;
const int red = 5;
const int yellow = 6;
const int green = 7;

void setup() {
  pinMode(red, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(yellow, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(green, OUTPUT);
  Serial.begin(9600);

  // Start Red
  digitalWrite(red, HIGH);
}

void loop() {
  int noise = analogRead(soundPin);

  if (noise > 500) {
    // COMMAND RECEIVED!

  }
}

void cycleLights() {
  // Go Green

  digitalWrite(green, HIGH);

  digitalWrite(green, LOW);
  digitalWrite(yellow, HIGH);
  delay(1000);

  digitalWrite(yellow, LOW);

  // Debounce (Don't trigger again immediately)

docs.title: 1. The Call to Adventure

  • GND -> GND

Note: We are using different pins than Mission 2.1. Pay attention!

docs.title: 4. The Logic
docs.text:
Step-by-Step:

  1. Pulse: Send a sound wave from the Trig pin.
  2. Listen: Count how long it takes to return to Echo.
  3. Calculate: Distance = Time x Speed.
  4. Decide:
    • IF Distance < 30cm (Intruder!) -> Buzzer ON.
    • ELSE (Clear) -> Buzzer OFF.

docs.title: The Code
docs.text:
// Mission 2.2: Intruder Alarm
const int trigPin = 3;
const int echoPin = 2;
const int buzzerPin = 4;

long duration;
int distance;

void setup() {
  pinMode(trigPin, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(echoPin, INPUT);
  pinMode(buzzerPin, OUTPUT);
  Serial.begin(9600);
}

void loop() {
  // 1. Send Ping
  digitalWrite(trigPin, LOW);
  delayMicroseconds(2);
  digitalWrite(trigPin, HIGH);
  delayMicroseconds(10);
  digitalWrite(trigPin, LOW);

  // 2. Read Echo
  duration = pulseIn(echoPin, HIGH);
  distance = duration * 0.034 / 2;

  // 3. Serial Monitor
  Serial.print("Range: ");
  Serial.println(distance);

  // 4. Security Logic
  if (distance < 30) {
    // INTRUDER DETECTED!
    digitalWrite(buzzerPin, HIGH);
    tone(buzzerPin, 1000); // 1KHz sound
    delay(200);
    noTone(buzzerPin);     // Pulse the sound
    delay(200); 
  } else {
    // SAFE
    digitalWrite(buzzerPin, LOW);
    noTone(buzzerPin);
  }
}

docs.title: 4. The Logic
docs.text:
Algorithms for the Road:

  1. Poll: Check distance every 100ms.
  2. Evaluate:
    • Zone 1 (< 10cm): STOP! (Red).
    • Zone 2 (< 30cm): CAUTION (Yellow).
    • Zone 3 (> 30cm): CLEAR (Green).

docs.title: The Code
docs.text:
// Mission 2.3: Smart Intersection
const int redPin = 5;
const int yellowPin = 6;
const int greenPin = 7;
const int trigPin = 12;
const int echoPin = 11;

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(9600);
  pinMode(redPin, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(yellowPin, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(greenPin, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(trigPin, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(echoPin, INPUT);
}

void loop() {
  // 1. Ping
  digitalWrite(trigPin, LOW);
  delayMicroseconds(2);
  digitalWrite(trigPin, HIGH);
  delayMicroseconds(10);
  digitalWrite(trigPin, LOW);

  // 2. Listen
  long duration = pulseIn(echoPin, HIGH);
  int distance = duration * 0.034 / 2;

  // 3. Reset Lights (Turn all off first)
  digitalWrite(redPin, LOW);
  digitalWrite(yellowPin, LOW);
  digitalWrite(greenPin, LOW);

  // 4. Decision Matrix
  if (distance < 10) {
    digitalWrite(redPin, HIGH); // STOP
  } else if (distance < 30) {
    digitalWrite(yellowPin, HIGH); // SLOW
  } else {
    digitalWrite(greenPin, HIGH); // GO
  }

  delay(100);
}

  • Rule: If closer than 20cm, show RED. Otherwise, show GREEN.

docs.title: The Code
docs.text:
// Mission 2.4: Visual Rangefinder
const int redPin = 3;
const int greenPin = 5;
const int bluePin = 6;
const int trigPin = 12;
const int echoPin = 11;

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(9600);
  pinMode(redPin, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(greenPin, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(bluePin, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(trigPin, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(echoPin, INPUT);
}

void loop() {
  // 1. Measure
  digitalWrite(trigPin, LOW);
  delayMicroseconds(2);
  digitalWrite(trigPin, HIGH);
  delayMicroseconds(10);
  digitalWrite(trigPin, LOW);

  long duration = pulseIn(echoPin, HIGH);
  int distance = duration * 0.034 / 2;

  // 2. Logic (Threshold = 20cm)
  if (distance < 20) {
    setColor(255, 0, 0); // Red
  } else {
    setColor(0, 255, 0); // Green
  }

  delay(100);
}

void setColor(int r, int g, int b) {
  analogWrite(redPin, r);
  analogWrite(greenPin, g);
  analogWrite(bluePin, b);
}

// Mission 2.5: The Controller
const int buttonPin = 2;
const int ledPin = 13;

void setup() {
  pinMode(ledPin, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(buttonPin, INPUT_PULLUP); // Activates internal resistor
}

void loop() {
  int state = digitalRead(buttonPin);

  if (state == LOW) {
    // Button Pressed
    digitalWrite(ledPin, HIGH);
  } else {
    // Button Released
    digitalWrite(ledPin, LOW);
  }
}

// Mission 2.6: Doorbell
const int buttonPin = 2;
const int buzzerPin = 3;

// Mission 2.7: Crosswalk
const int buttonPin = 2;
const int red = 5;
const int yellow = 6;
const int green = 7;

void setup() {
  pinMode(buttonPin, INPUT_PULLUP);
  pinMode(red, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(yellow, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(green, OUTPUT);

  // Start with Green
  digitalWrite(green, HIGH);
}

void loop() {
  int request = digitalRead(buttonPin);

  if (request == LOW) {
    // Pedestrian wants to cross!
    changeLights();
  }
}

void changeLights() {
  // 1. Slow down cars
  digitalWrite(green, LOW);
  digitalWrite(yellow, HIGH);
  delay(2000);

  // 2. Stop cars
  digitalWrite(yellow, LOW);
  digitalWrite(red, HIGH);

  // 3. Walk Time
  delay(5000); 

  // 4. Return to normal
  digitalWrite(red, LOW);
  digitalWrite(green, HIGH);
}

docs.title: 1. The Call to Adventure
docs.text: Static lights are boring. We want a light that changes to match our mood. Your mission is to build a "State Machine" that cycles through colors.

docs.title: 4. The Logic
docs.text:
We use a variable colorMode to remember where we are.

  • 0 = Red
  • 1 = Green
  • 2 = Blue
  • 3 = OFF

docs.title: The Code
docs.text:
// Mission 2.8: Mood Light
const int buttonPin = 2;
const int redPin = 3;
const int greenPin = 5;
const int bluePin = 6;

int colorMode = 0;       
int lastButtonState = HIGH; // Start HIGH (Not pressed)

void setup() {
  pinMode(redPin, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(greenPin, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(bluePin, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(buttonPin, INPUT_PULLUP);
}

void loop() {
  int buttonState = digitalRead(buttonPin);

  // Detect CLICK (High -> Low)
  if (buttonState == LOW && lastButtonState == HIGH) {
    colorMode++;
    if (colorMode > 3) colorMode = 0; // Reset loop
    delay(200); // Debounce
  }

  lastButtonState = buttonState;

  // Apply Color
  if (colorMode == 0) setColor(255, 0, 0);       // Red
  else if (colorMode == 1) setColor(0, 255, 0);  // Green
  else if (colorMode == 2) setColor(0, 0, 255);  // Blue
  else setColor(0, 0, 0);                        // OFF
}

void setColor(int r, int g, int b) {
  analogWrite(redPin, r);
  analogWrite(greenPin, g);
  analogWrite(bluePin, b);
}

docs.text:
Step-by-Step:

  1. Read the Light level (0-1023).
  2. Compare: Is it darker than our threshold? (e.g., < 300).
  3. Act: Turn LED HIGH or LOW.

docs.title: The Code
docs.text:
// Mission 2.9: Smart Streetlight
const int ldrPin = A0;
const int ledPin = 6;

void setup() {
  Serial.begin(9600);
  pinMode(ledPin, OUTPUT);
}

void loop() {
  int brightness = analogRead(ldrPin);
  Serial.println(brightness); // Calibrate using this number

  // Threshold: Adjust based on your room (cover sensor to test)
  if (brightness < 300) {
    digitalWrite(ledPin, HIGH); // Night time
  } else {
    digitalWrite(ledPin, LOW);  // Day time
  }
  delay(100);
}

docs.title: Mission 3.1: The City Dashboard
docs.text: Role: City Planner Objective: Build a visual status board to monitor critical infrastructure (like a Water Tower).

docs.title: Result Preview
docs.text: Green means SAFE. Red means DANGER (too close).

docs.title: 1. The Call to Adventure
docs.text:
In the Smart City, data is useless if humans can't read it. A City Mayor doesn't want to see "Distance = 3cm". They want to see "Green = Safe" or "Red = Danger".

We need a system that takes raw data (Distance) and converts it into a visual status update.

docs.title: 2. The Toolkit
docs.text:
• 1x Ultrasonic Sensor: The Monitor.
  • 1x Green LED: "Safe" Indicator.
  • 1x Red LED: "Danger" Indicator.
  • 2x Resistors (330 Ohm): Protection for LEDs.

docs.title: 3. The Blueprint
docs.text:
Construct the circuit on your breadboard:

  • Ultrasonic: Same as Mission 2.1 (Trig->9, Echo->10).
  • Red LED: Positive -> Pin 6.
  • Green LED: Positive -> Pin 7.

docs.title: 4. The Logic
docs.text:
We are building a State Machine. Here is the step-by-step logic:

  1. Measure: Ask the sensor for distance (in cm).
  2. Analyze:
    • IF distance < 10cm: Situation is CRITICAL.
    • ELSE: Situation is NORMAL.
  3. Display:
    • Critical: Turn Red LED ON, Green LED OFF.
    • Normal: Turn Green LED ON, Red LED OFF.

docs.title: The Code
docs.text:
// Mission 3.1: The City Dashboard
const int trigPin = 9;
const int echoPin = 10;
const int redLed = 6;
const int greenLed = 7;

long duration;
int distance;

void setup() {
  pinMode(trigPin, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(echoPin, INPUT);
  pinMode(redLed, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(greenLed, OUTPUT);
  Serial.begin(9600);
}

void loop() {
  // 1. Measure Distance
  digitalWrite(trigPin, LOW);
  delayMicroseconds(2);
  digitalWrite(trigPin, HIGH);
  delayMicroseconds(10);
  digitalWrite(trigPin, LOW);

  duration = pulseIn(echoPin, HIGH);
  distance = duration * 0.034 / 2;

  // 2. The Decision Logic
  if (distance < 10) { 
    // DANGER STATE (Water level too high!)
    digitalWrite(redLed, HIGH);
    digitalWrite(greenLed, LOW);
    Serial.println("STATUS: CRITICAL WARNING");
  } 
  else {
    // SAFE STATE
    digitalWrite(redLed, LOW);
    digitalWrite(greenLed, HIGH);
    Serial.println("STATUS: NORMAL");
  }

  delay(500); // Update twice a second
}

docs.title: 5. The Debrief
docs.text: Watch your dashboard. As you move your hand closer, the city's status should change instantly from Green to Red.

docs.title: 6. Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Both LEDs off?
  • Check if you added pinMode(OUTPUT) for both LEDs.
  • Ultrasonic not reading?
  • Note that we changed pins for this Mission (Trig is 9, Echo is 10). Did you move the wires?

docs.text:

  • Logic: Add an else if block.
  • if (distance < 10) -> Red
  • else if (distance < 20) -> Yellow
  • else -> Green

docs.title: Mission 3.2: The Silent Alarm
docs.text: Role: Security Systems Architect Objective: Protect the Vault. If anything gets too close, trigger the alarm.

docs.title: Result Preview

docs.title: 1. The Call to Adventure
docs.text: The city bank needs a new security system. Your mission is to build a "Proximity Alarm" that detects invisible intruders using sound waves.

docs.title: 2. The Toolkit
docs.text:
• 1x Ultrasonic Sensor (Eyes)
  • 1x Buzzer (Siren)
  • 1x Red LED (Warning Light)
  • 1x Arduino Uno (Brain)

docs.title: 3. The Blueprint
docs.text:
• Ultrasonic Trig: Pin 6
  • Ultrasonic Echo: Pin 7
  • Buzzer +: Pin 8
  • LED +: Pin 9
  • GND: Common Ground

docs.title: 4. The Logic
docs.text:
Algorithm:

  1. Ping: Send a sound wave.
  2. Listen: Measure how long it takes to return.
  3. Calculate: Distance = Time x Speed of Sound.
  4. Decide: If Distance < 20cm -> ALARM!

docs.title: The Code
docs.text:
// Mission 3.2: Smart Security System
const int trigPin = 6;
const int echoPin = 7;
const int buzzerPin = 8;
const int ledPin = 9;

void setup() {
  pinMode(trigPin, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(echoPin, INPUT);
  pinMode(buzzerPin, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(ledPin, OUTPUT);
  Serial.begin(9600);
}

void loop() {
  long duration, distance;

  // 1. Send Pulse
  digitalWrite(trigPin, LOW);
  delayMicroseconds(2);
  digitalWrite(trigPin, HIGH);
  delayMicroseconds(10);
  digitalWrite(trigPin, LOW);

  // 2. Measure Pulse
  duration = pulseIn(echoPin, HIGH);

  // 3. Calculate Distance (cm)
  distance = (duration / 2) / 29.1;

  Serial.print(distance);
  Serial.println(" cm");

  // 4. Security Logic
  if (distance > 0 && distance < 20) {
    // INTRUDER ALERT!
    digitalWrite(ledPin, HIGH);
    tone(buzzerPin, 1000); // 1 kHz sound
  } else {
    // Safe
    digitalWrite(ledPin, LOW);
    noTone(buzzerPin);
  }

  delay(100);
}

docs.title: 5. Upload & Test
docs.text:
1. Upload code.
  2. Place your hand far away (Safe).
  3. Move hand closer (< 20cm).
  4. BEEP! LED ON.

docs.title: 6. Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Alarm triggering constantly?
  • Ultrasonic sensors can be noisy. Ensure it's pointing at empty space.
  • Distance is 0?
  • Check VCC (5V) and GND connections on the sensor. 0 usually means "Unplugged".

docs.title: Mission 3.3: Adaptive Traffic System
docs.text: Role: Traffic Control Engineer Objective: Reduce traffic jams. The light should stay Green if no cars are waiting on the other side.

docs.title: Result Preview
docs.text: Car approaches (Ultrasonic < 10cm) -> Light turns Red to stop it? Or Green to let it go? Correction: Usually "Smart" means "Green for the busy lane". Let's assume the sensor is watching the "Cross Street". If car detected, give them Green.

docs.title: 1. The Call to Adventure
docs.text: Old traffic lights are dumb. They maintain Red even when no one is crossing. Your mission is to build a system that senses cars and changes the light dynamically.

docs.title: 2. The Toolkit
docs.text:
• 1x Ultrasonic Sensor (Vehicle Detector)
  • 1x Traffic Light Module
  • 1x Arduino Uno

docs.title: 3. The Blueprint
docs.text:

  • Ultrasonic Echo: Pin 10
  • Traffic Lights: 6 (R), 7 (Y), 8 (G)
  • GND: Common Ground

docs.title: 4. The Logic
docs.text:
Scenario: The sensor is on the "Main Road".

  1. Default: Red (Stop).
  2. Detection: If car arrives (Distance < 10cm).
  3. Action: Cycle Green -> Yellow -> Red.

docs.title: The Code
docs.text:
// Mission 3.3: Smart Traffic Light
const int trigPin = 9;
const int echoPin = 10;
const int red = 6;
const int yellow = 7;
const int green = 8;

void setup() {
  pinMode(trigPin, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(echoPin, INPUT);
  pinMode(red, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(yellow, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(green, OUTPUT);
  Serial.begin(9600);

  // Start Red
  digitalWrite(red, HIGH);
}

void loop() {
  long duration, distance;

  // Ping
  digitalWrite(trigPin, LOW); 
  delayMicroseconds(2);
  digitalWrite(trigPin, HIGH);
  delayMicroseconds(10);
  digitalWrite(trigPin, LOW);

  duration = pulseIn(echoPin, HIGH);
  distance = (duration / 2) / 29.1;

  Serial.println(distance);

  // If Car is waiting (< 10cm) AND currently Red
  if (distance > 0 && distance < 10) {
    // Give them the Green Light!
    triggerGreenSequence();
  }

  delay(100);
}

void triggerGreenSequence() {
  // Red OFF, Green ON
  digitalWrite(red, LOW);
  digitalWrite(green, HIGH);
  delay(5000); // 5 Seconds of Green

  // Green OFF, Yellow ON
  digitalWrite(green, LOW);
  digitalWrite(yellow, HIGH);
  delay(2000); // 2 Seconds of Caution

  // Yellow OFF, Red ON
  digitalWrite(yellow, LOW);
  digitalWrite(red, HIGH);

  delay(2000); // Safety pause
}

docs.title: 5. Upload & Test
docs.text:
1. Upload code.
  2. Red light should be ON.
  3. Move your hand in front of the ultrasonic sensor (Simulate "Car Arriving").
  4. Light should switch to Green, then Yellow, then back to Red.

docs.text:
• Nothing happens?

  • Check Serial Monitor for distance values.

docs.title: Mission 3.4: Adaptive Home Lighting
docs.text: Role: Smart Home Architect Objective: Lights that gently turn ON when it gets dark.

docs.title: Result Preview
docs.text: Sun sets -> Light turns ON.

docs.title: 1. The Call to Adventure
docs.text: Why fumble for switches in the dark? A smart home should know when you need light. Your mission is to use the LDR (Light Dependent Resistor) to control your room light automatically.

docs.title: 2. The Toolkit
docs.text:
• 1x LDR Sensor (Input)
  • 1x LED (Output)
  • 1x Resistor (10k Ohm or 220 Ohm depending on circuit)
  • 1x Arduino Uno

docs.title: 3. The Blueprint
docs.text:
• LDR Analog: Pin A0
  • LED Positive: Pin 6
  • LED Negative: GND
  • VCC/GND: 5V/GND

docs.title: 4. The Logic
docs.text:
Algorithm:

  1. Read Light Level.
  2. Logic: If Darkness Detected (< Threshold), Turn LED ON.
    • Note: The original legacy code had this backwards (> 500). Usually, low reading = dark.
  3. Bonus: Use analogWrite to fade it in!

docs.title: The Code
docs.text:
// Mission 3.4: Smart Bed Light
const int ldrPin = A0;
const int ledPin = 6;

void setup() {
  pinMode(ledPin, OUTPUT);
  Serial.begin(9600);
}

void loop() {
  int brightness = analogRead(ldrPin);
  Serial.print("Brightness: ");
  Serial.println(brightness);

  // If it's DARK (Low number)
  if (brightness < 300) { 
    digitalWrite(ledPin, HIGH); // Turn Light ON
  } else {
    digitalWrite(ledPin, LOW);  // Turn Light OFF
  }

  delay(200);
}

docs.title: 5. Upload & Test
docs.text:
1. Upload code.
  2. Cover the sensor. The light should turn ON.
  3. Uncover. The light should turn OFF.

docs.title: 6. Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Opposite behavior?
  • Change < 300 to > 300. Some LDR modules are wired differently (pull-up vs pull-down).
  • Flickering?
  • Add a small "buffer" (hysteresis) or just tweak the threshold.

docs.title: Mission 3.5: The Automated Garage
docs.text: Role: Parking Systems Engineer Objective: Build a barrier that opens automatically when a car arrives.

docs.title: Result Preview
docs.text: Car approaches -> RGB turns Red -> Barrier Opens -> Car Parks -> Barrier Closes -> RGB Green.

docs.title: 1. The Call to Adventure
docs.text: Manual garage doors are a hassle. Your mission is to use the Ultrasonic Sensor, Servo Motor, and RGB LED to build a fully automated parking system.

docs.title: 2. The Toolkit
docs.text:
• 1x Ultrasonic Sensor (Detector)
  • 1x Servo Motor (Barrier Gate)
  • 1x RGB LED (Status Light)
  • 1x Arduino Uno

docs.title: 3. The Blueprint
docs.text:
• Ultrasonic Trig: 6
  • Ultrasonic Echo: 7
  • Servo Control: 8
  • RGB Red: 9
  • RGB Green: 10
  • RGB Blue: 11
  • VCC/GND: As required.

docs.title: 4. The Logic
docs.text:
Algorithm:

  1. Check Distance.
  2. IF Car Detected (< 20cm):
    • RGB -> RED (Occupied/Busy).
    • Servo -> 0 degrees (Open Barrier).
    • Wait 5 seconds.
    • Servo -> 90 degrees (Close Barrier).
  3. ELSE (Empty):
    • RGB -> GREEN (Available).
    • Barrier stays Closed.

docs.title: The Code
docs.text:
// Mission 3.5: Automated Garage
#include <Servo.h>

const int trig = 6;
const int echo = 7;
const int servoPin = 8;
const int red = 9;
const int green = 10;
const int blue = 11;

Servo barrier;
long duration;
int distance;

void setup() {
  pinMode(trig, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(echo, INPUT);

  pinMode(red, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(green, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(blue, OUTPUT);

  barrier.attach(servoPin);
  barrier.write(90); // Closed

  Serial.begin(9600);
}

void loop() {
  // 1. Measure Distance
  digitalWrite(trig, LOW); delayMicroseconds(2);
  digitalWrite(trig, HIGH); delayMicroseconds(10);
  digitalWrite(trig, LOW);

  duration = pulseIn(echo, HIGH);
  distance = duration * 0.034 / 2;

  Serial.println(distance);

  // 2. Logic
  if (distance > 0 && distance < 20) {
    // Car Arriving!
    openBarrier();
  } else {
    // Vacant
    setRGB(0, 255, 0); // Green
    barrier.write(90); // Keep Closed
  }

  delay(200);
}

void openBarrier() {
  setRGB(255, 0, 0); // Red (Busy)
  barrier.write(0);  // Open!
  delay(5000);       // Wait for car to enter
  barrier.write(90); // Close
  delay(1000);
}

void setRGB(int r, int g, int b) {
  analogWrite(red, r);
  analogWrite(green, g);
  analogWrite(blue, b);
}

docs.title: 5. Upload & Test
docs.text:
1. Upload code.
  2. RG should be Green (Available).
  3. Move hand closer (< 20cm).
  4. RGB turns Red, Servo moves (Barrier Opens).

docs.title: 6. Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Servo jittery?
  • Servos need good power. If it twitches, try a separate 5V supply or ensure Arduino USB is fully powered.
  • RGB colors wrong?
  • Check 9, 10, 11 order.

docs.title: Mission 3.6: Voice Controlled Appliances
docs.text: Role: IoT Developer Objective: Control your home appliances (LED) with a clap.

docs.title: Result Preview
docs.text: Clap -> Light ON. Clap again -> Light OFF.

docs.title: 1. The Call to Adventure
docs.text: Imagine switching off your room light from your bed just by clapping. Your mission is to enable "Hands-Free" control.

docs.title: 2. The Toolkit
docs.text:
• 1x Sound Sensor (Input)
  • 1x LED (Output)
  • 1x Arduino Uno

docs.title: 3. The Blueprint
docs.text:
• Sound Pin: 2 (Digital Output from module)
  • LED: 6
  • VCC/GND: 5V/GND

docs.title: 4. The Logic
docs.text:
Algorithm:

  1. Read Sensor: Digital input.
  2. Toggle Logic: state =! state (If 1, make 0. If 0, make 1).
  3. Debounce: Wait for the sound to stop before reading again.

docs.title: The Code
docs.text:
// Mission 3.6: Voice Control
const int soundPin = 2; // Digital Pin (Adjust sensitivity on module)
const int ledPin = 6;

int state = LOW;

void setup() {
  pinMode(soundPin, INPUT);
  pinMode(ledPin, OUTPUT);
}

void loop() {
  int noise = digitalRead(soundPin);

  if (noise == HIGH) {
    // Detected Sound
    state = !state; // Toggle (Flip)
    digitalWrite(ledPin, state);
    delay(500); // Wait for silence (Debounce)
  }
}

docs.title: 5. Upload & Test
docs.text:
1. Upload code.
  2. Clap loudly. Light should toggle.
  3. Sensitivity: You MUST adjust the blue potentiometer on the sensor module until the LED on the module flickers ONLY when you clap.

docs.title: 6. Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Light just flickers randomlly?
  • Sensor is too sensitive. Turn the screw.
  • Won't turn off?
  • Increase delay to 1000 to prevent "Double switching".

Step 2: The Interface When it opens, you will see a window like this. This is where you will write your code.

docs.title: Key Areas to Know
docs.text:
• void setup(): This runs once when you turn on the board. We use it to tell the board what devices are connected (like "I have an LED on pin 6").
  • void loop(): This runs forever in a circle. This is where the magic happens (like "Turn LED on... wait... turn off").

docs.title: 2. Preparing the Code Space
docs.text:
To make coding easier, let's make some space. Click before void setup() and press Enter a few times to create a blank space at the top.

Why? We use this top space to give names to our pins (e.g., int led = 6;). It makes code easier to read!

docs.title: 3. Comments (Notes for Humans)
docs.text:
You will often see lines starting with //. These are Comments.

  • The computer ignores them.
  • They are there to help YOU understand what the code does.
// This is a comment. It does nothing to the board.
pinMode(6, OUTPUT); // This sets pin 6 as an output

docs.title: 4. Connecting Your Board
docs.text:
Now, let's connect your STEMAIDE board to the computer.

Step 1: Plug it in Connect the blue USB cable to the Arduino and your USB port.

Step 2: Select Board Go to Tools > Board > Arduino Uno.

Step 3: Select Port Go to Tools > Port and select the one that says Arduino Uno (e.g., COM3, COM5, /dev/tty...).

Note: If you don't see "Arduino Uno" next to a port, try unplugging and replugging the cable.

docs.title: 5. Saving & Uploading
docs.text:
Once you have written code (we'll do that in the next chapter!), you need to send it to the board.

  1. Verify (Check): Click the Checkmark icon. This checks for spelling mistakes in your code.
  2. Upload (Send): Click the Arrow icon. This sends the code to the board.

Success! When you see "Done uploading" at the bottom, your code is running on the board!

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
This guide is for Educators, Engineers, and Advanced Students who want to add new projects to the STEMAIDE Kit documentation. We call these "Missions".

Goal: Transform complex electronic concepts into engaging, story-driven challenges.

docs.title: 1. The Narrative Structure
docs.text:
Every new project must follow the Innovator's Journey format:

  1. The Call to Adventure (Problem): What real-world problem are we solving? (e.g., Dark streets, Crashes).
  2. The Toolkit (Components): What parts do we need?
  3. The Blueprint (Wiring): Clear diagrams.
  4. The Logic (Code): Explain the concept, not just the syntax.
  5. The Debrief (Challenge): A follow-up task to test understanding.

docs.title: 2. Style Guide
docs.text:
• Tone: Encouraging, Professional, African-Centric.
  • Role: Treat the reader as a "Lead Engineer" or "Innovator", not a student.
  • Code: Use clear variable names (int redPin = 5 NOT int r = 5).

docs.title: 3. How to Submit
docs.text:
1. Fork the repository.
  2. Create a new Markdown file in the appropriate Level folder (e.g., 3.0/3.7.Smart_Irrigation).
  3. Images: Put diagrams in assets/.
  4. Submit a Pull Request.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: This handbook is your field guide to the STEMAIDE Kit. While the "Missions" (Level 1, 2, 3) teach you how to build specific projects, this guide provides the technical reference data you might need along the way.

docs.title: 1. Safety First
docs.text:
Before you build, remember the Innovator's Code:

  1. Never connect wires while the board is plugged into the computer.
  2. Double-check your wiring (especially VCC and GND) before powering up.
  3. Keep it tidy. A messy circuit is hard to debug.

docs.title: Digital Outputs (Actuators)
docs.text:
• LEDs: Light Emitting Diodes. Beware of polarity (Long leg is +).
  • Buzzer: Makes sound. Active buzzers need only 5V; Passive buzzers need a signal.
  • Traffic Light Module: Pins are R, Y, G, GND.

docs.title: Analog Inputs (Sensors)
docs.text:
• LDR (Light Dependent Resistor): Resistance changes with light. Good for "Smart Street Lights".
  • Potentiometer: A knob that changes resistance. Good for dials and volume.

docs.title: Digital Inputs
docs.text: • Push Button: Connects two points when pressed. Use INPUT_PULLUP to make wiring easier.

docs.title: Smart Modules
docs.text:
• Ultrasonic Sensor (HC-SR04): Measures distance using sound. Echolocation!
  • Servo Motor: Moves to a specific angle (0-180 degrees).

docs.title: 3. Common Troubleshooting
docs.text:
"My Code Won't Upload!"

  • Check the USB Cable. Is it plugged in firmly?
  • Check Tools > Board. Is "Arduino Uno" selected?
  • Check Tools > Port. Is the correct COM port selected?

"The circuit isn't working!"

  • Check GND. Is everything connected to Ground?
  • Check Pin Numbers. Did you plug the LED into Pin 6 but program Pin 5?
  • Check Polarity. Are your LEDs plugged in backwards?
